cards.b: Force × perpendicular distance from the pivot; a measure of its turning effect.
For an object in equilibrium, the clockwise moment about a pivot = the anticlockwise moment about the same pivot.
No resultant force and no resultant moment.
Distance from the pivot at right angles to the line of action of the force.

cards.f: Why is a door handle far from the hinges?
cards.b: Bigger distance from the pivot gives a bigger moment for the same force, so the door is easier to turn.
The point through which the weight of an object acts.

cards.f: Where is the centre of gravity of a uniform block, sphere or cylinder?
Find the centre of gravity of an irregular lamina
cards.b: Hang it from a pin at three holes in turn with a plumb line; mark each vertical line; the lines cross at the centre of gravity.
The vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

cards.f: How to make an object more stable
cards.b: Lower the centre of gravity and widen the base.
Force per unit area: p = F ÷ A. Unit Pa = N/m².

cards.f: Why do knives and drawing pins have a small area at the tip?
cards.b: Small area gives a large pressure for the same force.

cards.f: Why does a pivot reaction force not appear when taking moments about the pivot?
cards.b: Its distance from the pivot is zero, so its moment is zero.

gaps.s: Moment = force × ___ distance from the pivot.
The principle of moments says that the clockwise moment equals the ___ moment.
A force of 20 N acts 0.30 m from a pivot. The moment is ___ N m.
A 4.0 N weight is 15 cm left of a pivot. A weight 10 cm right of the pivot balances the beam, so it is ___ N.
A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.50 m², giving a pressure of ___ Pa.
A tall object with a high centre of gravity is ___ stable than a low one of the same base.
A plumb line hangs in a straight ___ line when at rest.

short.q: A uniform beam is balanced with a 30 N weight 0.40 m from the pivot on one side. Calculate the force that balances it at 0.60 m on the other side.
Describe how to find the centre of gravity of an irregular cardboard lamina.
short.model: Make holes near the edge. Hang the lamina from a pin through one hole with a plumb line, mark the vertical line, and repeat for other holes. The centre of gravity is where the lines cross.
points: suspend freely from a pin through a hole
use plumb line and mark the vertical
lines cross at centre of gravity

short.q: Explain why a racing car is designed with a low centre of gravity and a wide wheelbase.
short.model: This makes it hard to topple: the line from the centre of gravity must move further to fall outside the base.

short.q: A box weighs 60 N and rests on a face of area 0.20 m². Calculate the pressure on the table.
Explain why snowshoes stop a person sinking into snow.
short.model: Snowshoes spread the weight over a larger area, so the pressure (force ÷ area) on the snow is smaller.
